items.title: Ampersand from Humans& now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: Ampersand from Humans& is now available on AI Gateway for free through November 13, 2026. Ampersand is a language model built to take part in group conversations, such as a team chat, and to decide on each turn whether to speak or stay quiet. It is designed to understand individual and shared goals, help people work through disagreements, and recognize when a contribution would be useful. That can mean asking a clarifying question, sharing relevant context, or waiting while people respond to one another. Your application exposes these actions as caller-defined function tools . send_message delivers a contribution, while pass leaves the conversation quiet until the next human message. Your application executes both tools and records their results. Leave tool choice at its default, since Ampersand accepts auto and none but rejects required and named tool choices. Call it through the AI SDK , the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API , or a coding agent. Use humansand/ampersand-v0.1 as the model name: The first human message invites a contribution; the second asks Ampersand to wait. In a chat application, call the handler when a new human message arrives. Handling pass records the waiting action without posting a message or starting another model turn. For a deployed chat application, persist the response, history, and delivery receipts in durable storage. Retry uncertain delivery with the saved action and the same receipt, process messages sequentially per conversation, and check conversation access before posting. To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select humansand/ampersand-v0.1 in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Ampersand in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

items.summary: この記事で学ぶこと #29 では、ログインの印（トークン）をどこに置くかを実測しました。そのとき「ページに悪意あるスクリプトが混入する攻撃（XSS）」という言葉が何度も出てきて、詳しくは今回、と先送りにしていました。今回はそれを正面から扱います。XSSはフロントエンドで一番多い脆弱性です。そして幸いなことに、Vue は既定でその大半を防いでくれています。何を自動で守ってくれて、どこに自分で穴を開けてしまうのか、全部実測して境界をはっきりさせます。 XSSが「人の書いた文字を命令として実行させてしまう」攻撃だと、具体例で説明できる Vue の {{ }} が自動でやってくれること、v...
items.titleJa: 35日でフロントエンドの基礎を完全に理解する #30 - フロントエンドのセキュリティ（XSS・CSP・サニタイズ・依存の脆弱性）
items.summaryJa: XSSは、利用者が入力した文字列をそのまま画面に出すと、文字として表示すべきなのにブラウザへ命令として解釈させてしまう攻撃です。信頼できない入力をHTMLとして出力する瞬間が最も警戒すべき境界となります。Vueの {{ }} は自動でエスケープされ、<img…> のような文字列はそのまま表示され、動作は起きませんが、v-html は生のHTMLをそのまま解釈させるため、攻撃コードが動く可能性があります。どうしても表示したい場合は DOMPurify などでサニタイズした上で渡すべきです。なお、CSP や npm audit による依存関係の点検を重ねることで、複数枚の防御壁を積み上げる多層防御が実現します。

items.title: How Zapier turns ideas into working software in hours with Vercel
items.summary: Zapier on Vercel Interactive partner demos in under two hours with v0, replacing a process that could take weeks First versions of three internal applications, each built in one day A shared daily briefing for more than 60 marketers, replacing individual efforts to assemble the same information 3.3 million sandboxes created in one month, isolating the code execution behind Zapier’s AI workloads Before the industry had a word for agents, Zapier was building them. Today Zapier is the AI orchestration platform connecting AI to the workflows, data, and systems businesses use every day. Zapier has been a Vercel customer since they began using Vercel for web experiences several years ago. They stayed, and expanded, because every team that needed to ship quickly found the same answer: speed, with the security guardrails already in place. As they grew, so did their adoption of Vercel as more teams found new uses for the platform. Today, Vercel supports work across engineering, partnerships, and marketing, from customer-facing AI to interactive partner demos and internal applications. The needs vary by team, but the priority is getting useful work into people’s hands quickly. A backend engineer can create an interactive demo of an integration inside a partner’s product. In marketing, a former product marketer with no prior deployment experience can share tools containing sensitive information through a company-approved environment and keep improving them as colleagues use them. Zapier’s teams are moving faster and doing more than they could before. When the next launch comes around, building on Vercel is a given. From weeks of prototype work to a demo in under two hours Every partnership Zapier signs extends what its customers can automate. The Powered by Zapier team is how those partnerships become product, helping SaaS and AI companies embed Zapier’s automation capabilities directly into their own tools, so users can automate without ever leaving the partner’s app. The stakes are high, because Zapier relies on this team to make its platform the entry point to all the software in the world. The problem was speed: collaborating outside the organization took forever, with every prototype requiring screenshots, design time, and frontend resources, and weeks could pass before a partner saw anything clickable. With v0 , the team can create a fully interactive, multi-view prototype in under two hours, showing an embedded Zapier experience inside the partner’s own product. Chu’s background is in backend development, not frontend engineering or design, but v0 lets her build these experiences without coordinating a separate design and frontend effort for every partner conversation. Partners can click through the flow and share it with colleagues, using the prototype as a blueprint for implementation alongside the API documentation. Sharing sensitive internal data securely In marketing, Joe Stych set out to make the team’s scattered knowledge easier to use. He had spent years in product marketing before becoming a agentic go-to-market engineer, but had never worked out of a Git repository or deployed an application. At an internal hackathon, he built Marketing Hive, a shared source for positioning, messaging, personas, and competitive intelligence. Sharing his local prototype meant making sensitive information accessible to colleagues without exposing it to everyone else. “The Hive holds our positioning, personas, and competitive intel, so I couldn't just send people a link. On Vercel it was behind our SSO from the first deploy, so I could share it without exposing it” says Joe Stych, Senior Lead, Agentic GTM at Zapier. Zapier’s data and security teams had already endorsed Vercel. Stych deployed through the company’s approved internal tooling environment, with access gated behind Zapier’s single sign-on. He develops in Cursor and keeps code and source material in GitLab, where changes trigger Vercel builds and deployments . If an update needs to be undone, he can roll back the deployment . The first versions of three of his internal applications took about a day each. In roughly two months, a hackathon project had grown into production software used across marketing. It was built by someone who had never deployed anything before. Internal apps for marketing and sales Marketing Hive holds the knowledge. Marketing OS puts it to work. It gives more than 60 marketers a daily briefing in Slack and a dashboard with what changed across marketing, one update from each team, a win worth celebrating, and progress against goals. Each marketer can start from the briefing instead of assembling the same information from separate channels. “The first five minutes of your day, you need to look at the Marketing OS update,” says Dan Slagen, Zapier’s CMO. Readers mark what they found useful, helping Stych prioritize improvements. The briefings also spark discussions in a marketing channel open to everyone at the company. Stych is building a sales coaching application that brings together account context and industry messaging before a call. Afterward, it reviews the Gong recording to highlight what worked and suggest changes to the talk track. For the internal applications, he checks reported numbers and the evidence behind claimed insights. Decisions about positioning remain with people, and he says additional safeguards will come before agents publish without human review. Model access and isolated code execution Beyond Marketing OS, a separate team at Zapier uses AI Gateway to send requests to AI models on behalf of customers using Zapier products. A common endpoint lets an application change or add models without maintaining a separate integration for each provider. Failover gives requests another route when a provider cannot serve them, while unified reporting lets a team see their usage across providers in once place. What's next Zapier’s relationship with Vercel began with web experiences and expanded as the company grew, with more teams finding uses for the platform as their needs changed. Today its role spans the software Zapier runs for customers and the tools its people build for one another, and every thread is still widening. The clearest picture of where it leads is in marketing, where other teams are starting to borrow the pattern. The goal is more versions across the company, and perhaps a Revenue OS for Zapier’s customer-facing teams next, each built the way the first one was, by someone close to the problem. First comes trust. Stych still checks reported numbers and the evidence behind claimed insights, and additional safeguards will come before agents publish without human review. Across all of it, Vercel helps Zapier put useful work into people’s hands and keep adapting it to the needs of the business. Read more

items.title: How OpenEvidence scales medical search for 650K doctors
items.summary: OpenEvidence on Vercel Serves 650,000 doctors with medical search Completes production deployments in about five minutes Absorbs traffic spikes without additional capacity provisioning Reduced serverless spend by 90% with Fluid compute Updates doctor- and patient-facing applications independently OpenEvidence helps physicians find medical evidence during care, whether they’re checking a dosage on intensive care rounds or handling a case outside their specialty without a specialist nearby. Answers draw on peer-reviewed literature and include citations, so doctors can examine the sources behind them. OpenEvidence’s small team began using Vercel to get early experiments online and kept that workflow as the product grew, relying on the platform to handle web deployments and capacity. Building software physicians depend on The stakes are different when software helps inform medical decisions. An incorrect answer can affect how a doctor treats a patient, while an unavailable application can cut off access to evidence when it is needed. OpenEvidence supported more than 20 million clinical consultations in January 2026 . The company also reported that more than 100 million Americans were treated by doctors using OpenEvidence in 2025 . "Honestly, life or death is not inaccurate," says Kush Khosla, Engineering Lead at OpenEvidence. "We operate in situations where it's an ER and they really need to know what's going on. Uptime is very, very important to us." "A lot of doctors and medical professionals are used to really outdated software," says Andy Yoon, Engineering Lead at OpenEvidence. A more modern experience still needs to meet physicians' expectations of speed, stability, clarity, and information they can trust. The small team needs a way to test updates to the web application before putting them into production and to roll back if something goes wrong. Keeping releases simple as the audience grows Andy recalls why Vercel suited the team he joined at OpenEvidence. "I was pretty much the only engineer on our team coming from an actual frontend background," he says. "Most of our team works in Python and machine learning." He adds, "Given the makeup of our engineering team, Vercel really scaled with our needs so well." The team builds its physician-facing web application with the Next.js framework . When engineers push changes to a development branch, Vercel builds and deploys a preview , giving them a link they can use for live demos and share with colleagues to try new features. Pushing or merging into the production branch then triggers the production build and deployment. If a release needs reverting, the team can roll back to a previous deployment . That workflow lets the team release multiple times a day, with each change becoming available to a physician audience that Kush thinks about whenever he ships something: More doctors without more provisioning Keeping that application available means handling demand the team can’t always anticipate. Andy was scrolling through Slack when he saw the message that OpenEvidence had gone viral on TikTok, reaching around two million views in under a week. He watched traffic climb and checked the logs. Response times stayed fast and error rates remained near zero , and with no additional capacity to provision, he went back to his work. Beyond sudden spikes, the team has accommodated sustained growth without rebuilding the web application. "Not once have I had to think, now that we have five times as many doctors, what's happening to page loads or time to first paint," Kush says. "The scaling has happened so naturally that we end up focusing on other things." A 90% drop in serverless spend As usage grew, VP of Engineering Micah Smith was watching compute costs. The team enabled Fluid compute for its functions on Vercel, and Micah described the result alongside the wider infrastructure budget: "We reduced our serverless spend by 90% while maintaining the same performance, and even as we've scaled up to 1000x growth, Vercel is less than 5% of our overall infra spend." Fluid compute lets multiple requests share a running function instance, so it can handle other work while a request waits for another service, such as a database or an AI backend, to respond. With Active CPU pricing , that waiting time doesn’t incur CPU charges, though memory remains billed while requests are in progress. A familiar workflow for a new audience Take Home, OpenEvidence’s first patient-facing application, lets a doctor translate a clinical answer into plain language and share it with a patient, who logs in to review and save the evidence. Clinical-trial matching is also part of the application’s planned direction. To support this expansion, the team uses a pattern established through dozens of early proofs of concept, each deployed as its own Vercel project with a custom domain. Stakeholders could open those applications and test the workflows for themselves. Getting new projects online in minutes helped the team find product-market fit and made it easier to win early enterprise partnerships. Take Home has its own project and domain too, so engineers can update the patient experience without deploying the other applications. With Take Home, evidence that helps a doctor during a consultation can become something a patient returns to afterward. About OpenEvidence: OpenEvidence helps healthcare professionals find medical evidence at the point of care, with answers sourced, cited, and grounded in peer-reviewed literature. Physicians use it daily across more than 10,000 hospitals and medical centers in the United States. Its mission is to help doctors save lives and improve patient care. Learn more at openevidence.com . Read more

items.title: Vercel MCP now supports Client ID Metadata Documents
items.summary: Any MCP client can now ask to connect to Vercel MCP . You still log in and approve each connection, but the client no longer has to be reviewed by Vercel first. Previously, Vercel reviewed and allowlisted each client and its redirect URIs by hand, and anything not on the list was rejected. To connect, a client publishes a Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD), a JSON file on its own domain that describes it, and uses that file's HTTPS URL as its OAuth client_id . This follows the MCP authorization spec, which now recommends CIMD over Dynamic Client Registration. Because Vercel hasn't reviewed these clients, the consent screen shows where each one comes from: its name, its logo, and the hostname that serves its metadata document, for example "Claude Code by claude.ai". CIMD clients don't get the Vercel verified badge, so the hostname is what you're trusting when you approve. Apps already registered with Vercel are unchanged. Read the Vercel MCP documentation to connect your client. Read more

items.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
items.summary: OpenAI’s Grid Protectors Program will work with utilities to help future compute campuses support grid reliability and protect consumer electricity costs.
items.titleJa: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
items.summaryJa: OpenAIのGrid Protectors Programは、将来の計算拠点が電力網の安定性を支え、消費者の電力コストを保護するため、電力事業者と協力して機能する。gridの信頼性確保と料金抑制を目的としている。
